implementation.client: SessionScreen computes identity-editing state once for view/input. ClearInput and Escape clear the username only before a login attempt; prompted responses remain zeroizing Secret storage. Connecting/verifying disable editing; lock identities stay fixed.
implementation.framework: run_without_ipc disables local command/inspection IPC for ordinary surfaces. Polkit selects it; the greeter compatibility entry point delegates to it. run_locked retains the authenticated session-lock gate.
implementation.lifecycle: State teardown drops GPU surfaces before Wayland roles and flushes queued destruction while the connection remains live, including error returns. Cleanup never authorizes unlock.
implementation.adapters: PAM, greetd and libpolkit-agent remain the trusted authentication authorities. Domain contracts and operating-system policy are unchanged.

reproduced_before_fix.retained_username: Regression reproduced the previous ClearInput failure before the active-field fix.
reproduced_before_fix.interpretation: A visually closed dialog still retained an empty compositor surface in the long-lived agent. The final native regression requires zero surfaces before the next request.

visual.scope: Existing lock/login/permission views at 1x/2x in both palettes pass on software and hardware Vulkan at the field-routing checkpoint. Later changes affect runtime entry/teardown; these views and rendering references are unchanged.

core_ci.final_evidence_head: Tracked on PR #37; the evidence commit requires its own checks.

deployment.linked_runtime_scope: Only authentication clients were rebuilt and installed. Other installed clients retain their existing linked runtime until rebuilt.

pending: Review and merge of PR #37 and its parent stack; final evidence-head CI is tracked on the PR.

Production authentication/PAM and authority-cancellation audit, native denied-lock/password recovery, agent/service failures, suspend/resume and physical lock/driver-fault acceptance remain unverified by this focused milestone.
General IPC-enabled clients and all other consumers need a rebuilt release to inherit the new runtime teardown; this deployment covers only the three authentication clients.
RSS below 200 MiB, active-overlay and image-decoding peaks, actual GPU allocations, hardware pacing, long idle and fault recovery remain open. No new performance measurements are claimed.

Remaining OS controls/tray, physical audio/networking and secret-agent/enterprise provisioning, per-output/fractional geometry, shaping/IME/accessibility, richer application/dock/widget/notification/settings behavior, packaging/migrations and rollback acceptance remain in docs/implementation-status.json.
